title: Durable, high-bandwidth two-way neural interface

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a neural interface that can reliably read intended actions and return useful sensory information through neural stimulation over years of everyday use. Its outward channel would translate neural activity into communication or control of a physical or virtual hand. Its inward channel would provide sensory feedback that helps the user guide those actions. Durability means preserving safe, useful function through changing neural signals, repeated use and practical maintenance. High bandwidth means enough selective, usable information to support the intended tasks; electrode count or raw data rate alone would not establish that capability. This is a synthesis of the proposed concept, not an achieved result.

The supplied study demonstrates an important part of this architecture: an implanted intracortical brain–computer interface decoded attempted speech and right-hand motor imagery into speech output, cursor movement and mouse clicks during extended home use. It did not demonstrate neural sensory stimulation. Combining multiple decoded outputs therefore establishes multimodal control, but does not by itself establish a two-way neural interface.

significance.text: Reliable everyday decoding can give people with severe paralysis and speech impairment useful ways to communicate and operate digital tools. Card and colleagues provide a concrete basis for this significance: one participant used speech and cursor decoding at home without researcher supervision after care-partner setup. The advance matters because useful assistive function must survive daily use beyond scheduled laboratory sessions.

Conditional impact synthesis: adding durable neural sensory feedback and sufficiently capable hand control could extend communication and digital access into sustained closed-loop interaction. Feedback that reliably informs the user about the controlled hand could improve manipulation and reduce the effort needed to monitor actions. If these benefits generalized across many users, the result could be a transformative assistive capability. Reduced dependence on caregivers or broader participation in work and daily activities would remain downstream possibilities requiring direct evaluation.

Limits of the proposed impact: this would be a task-specific interface to selected neural signals and stimulation targets, not evidence of arbitrary thought reading or a treatment for every neurological condition. Useful artificial sensation would also not automatically reproduce natural sensation in its full richness. Two-dimensional cursor control cannot be treated as evidence of dexterous hand restoration, and success in one participant cannot establish broad clinical applicability.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing integrated capability is sustained, practical two-way function: selective neural recording, stable decoding, useful control and beneficial neural sensory stimulation working together over long periods. The supplied study identifies chronic neural signal variability and the need for recording sensors and decoding performance to remain stable. Calibration, wired access, setup and portability also constrain the demonstrated recording-based system. These are concrete obstacles to making everyday operation dependable and convenient.

Engineering synthesis: the sensory channel would need stimulation that conveys interpretable, task-relevant information with adequate selectivity, while preserving useful recording and control. The system would need to maintain that relationship as signals and user strategies change. Electrode design, recording and stimulation electronics, signal processing, decoding, power and system integration must jointly support this goal. More channels would be valuable only insofar as they improve reliable functional information and user benefit.

Additional barriers retained from the proposed concept include tissue response, access to suitable neural populations, safe long-term stimulation and practical power provision. Their importance and tractability for a particular architecture cannot be assessed from the supplied study alone. Its recording and decoding results do not establish chronic stimulation safety, quantify tissue-response limits or resolve the full power problem. The authors also did not systematically assess user fatigue or long-term device wear, limiting what sustained decoding performance can establish about overall durability.

current_state.text: In “Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control,” reported on 15 June 2026, Nicholas S. Card and colleagues described one man with paralysis and severe dysarthria due to ALS using the system at home nearly every day for 19 months. He accumulated more than 3,800 hours of independent use. Independence here meant operation without researcher supervision; trained care partners assisted with putting on and removing hardware and initializing software. It did not mean assistance-free setup or removal.

In prompted speech-copy benchmarks, silent speech averaged 49.7 words per minute with reported word accuracy of 96.5%. Vocalized speech averaged 30.6 words per minute with accuracy exceeding 99%. These figures describe the reported benchmark conditions and should not be presented as measured accuracy during unrestricted everyday conversation. The distinction preserves the strength of the demonstrated performance without extending it to an unevaluated setting.

Two additional decoders translated right-hand motor imagery into two-dimensional cursor control and discrete mouse clicks. A gaze-controlled toggle activated these decoders, and gaze tracking assisted interface use. The study therefore demonstrated practical speech and cursor control through an interface combining neural decoding with other interaction support. It did not demonstrate dexterous physical-hand control or a neural sensory return channel.

The demonstrated duration and extensive home use are substantial evidence of sustained assistive decoding in this participant. Generalizability to other people, implant sites, intracortical electrode types and neurological conditions remained unknown. Continued decoding performance also cannot substitute for the systematic assessments of fatigue and long-term device wear that the study did not perform. These limits leave broader durability and two-way restoration unresolved; they do not negate the reported home-use result.

Evidence scope: according to the supplied research and validated review, the accessible article text was inspected, including full main text, methods and references, with no reported extraction truncation. The publisher PDF failed to open, so the numerical account here rests on the reviewed article text rather than a separate PDF or figure inspection. The supplied search record was empty, leaving field-wide freshness unassessed, including the review's referenced 1 November 2026 assessment date. This record supports the dated June 2026 result but cannot establish whether subsequent work achieved additional capabilities.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: an appropriately designed clinical program should show years of everyday use in a diverse cohort, combining communication with control of a physical or virtual hand and an explicit neural sensory stimulation channel. Feedback should measurably improve prespecified task performance or another meaningful functional outcome compared with an appropriate control condition. The duration, cohort composition and required improvement would be proposed evaluation choices, not established standards supplied by the article.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed operational definitions: independence should specify permitted care-partner help, including setup, removal, software initialization, calibration and troubleshooting. Trials should distinguish researcher-free operation from assistance-free use and report how much help is required in practice. Functional endpoints should separate prompted benchmarks from spontaneous communication and everyday control, and should account for supporting inputs such as gaze tracking.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed operational definitions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and safety assessment: prespecify long-term safety, functional benefit, user control, fatigue, maintenance burden and device-wear outcomes. Track performance drift, calibration needs, interruptions, repairs and stimulation tolerability alongside successful task use. Users should be able to initiate and stop operation and retain meaningful control over outputs. Practical success should include a maintenance and support burden compatible with the intended home setting.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed durability and safety assessment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility boundary: demonstrate repeatable benefit across participants, repeated sessions and relevant everyday environments, with sufficiently documented hardware, decoding, stimulation and assistance procedures to support independent evaluation. Report the tested conditions and failures explicitly. A finite clinical program could establish convincing breadth within those boundaries; it could not establish literal universality across people, neural targets, tasks or diseases.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster comparison synthesis: ELE-08, “Manufacturable ultra-low-voltage switching for general-purpose electronics,” and ELE-11, “Integrated photonic-electronic computing with broad system advantage,” concern potential enabling electronics and computation. Improvements in those areas could help neural-interface processing or power budgets, but would not establish safe chronic recording, interpretable sensory stimulation or clinical benefit. ELE-06 is defined by durable two-way function at the neural and user interface.

Roster comparison synthesis: ELE-07, “Infrastructure-scale wireless electrical power delivery,” and ELE-10, “Broadly deployable, maintenance-free ambient-powered sensing,” overlap with questions of power provision, sensing and maintenance. Their scales and operating environments differ from implanted neural systems. Neither infrastructure-scale wireless power nor ambient-powered sensing would by itself resolve the selectivity, chronic operation and functional-feedback requirements of ELE-06.

Roster comparison synthesis: ELE-01, “Practical ambient-temperature superconducting conductors,” ELE-05, “Cheap, scalable storage for weeks to seasons of electrical supply,” and ELE-09, “Resilient, self-restoring power networks,” address electrical conduction, energy supply and grid reliability. Those advances could contribute to the wider infrastructure supporting assistive technologies, but their completion would not demonstrate a neural interface. ELE-06 has distinct biological, clinical and interaction requirements.

Roster comparison synthesis: ELE-02, “Fault-tolerant quantum computer with useful, scalable logical computation,” ELE-03, “A long-distance quantum repeater network,” and ELE-04, “Practical, energy-recovering reversible computing,” address different computation or communication capabilities. The supplied material establishes no requirement that ELE-06 depend on these breakthroughs. Neural decoding and sensory stimulation should be evaluated through their own functional and clinical evidence, without importing claims of quantum or reversible-computing advantage.

Disciplinary synthesis: ELE-06 also overlaps neuroscience, clinical medicine, rehabilitation and robotics. Electrical engineering supplies electrodes, electronics, signal processing, power and integration; clinical and behavioral evaluation must establish safety and useful function. These relationships explain its interdisciplinary character while preserving its identity as a durable, high-bandwidth two-way neural interface.

change_log.change: Preserved ELE-06 and its title while explicitly defining recording-based control and neural sensory stimulation as the two directions.
change_log.reason: The supplied study demonstrates multiple decoded outputs, but those outputs alone do not fulfill the concept's two-way identity.

change_log.change: Expanded the dated home-use account to include 19 months, more than 3,800 hours, care-partner setup and removal, and gaze-assisted interaction.
change_log.reason: These reviewed details establish the scale of demonstrated use and clarify the practical meaning of independence.

change_log.change: Retained 49.7 words per minute and 96.5% word accuracy for silent speech, added the reviewed vocalized-speech results, and identified both as prompted benchmarks.
change_log.reason: The numbers are supported, but unrestricted conversational accuracy was not established by those benchmarks.

change_log.change: Distinguished demonstrated signal variability, calibration and home-use constraints from incompletely evidenced tissue-response, power and chronic-stimulation barriers.
change_log.reason: The broader engineering questions remain relevant without being presented as fully established by the single supplied study.

change_log.change: Integrated the limitations on generalizability, fatigue assessment and long-term device-wear assessment.
change_log.reason: Sustained decoding performance supports the reported achievement but cannot answer all questions about durability or clinical applicability.

change_log.change: Made proposed completion criteria explicit about neural stimulation, assistance, functional endpoints, safety, maintenance and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: These distinctions make a future demonstration assessable without presenting proposed thresholds as established standards.

change_log.change: Preserved conditional assistive significance and bounded claims about dexterity, sensory restoration and downstream independence.
change_log.reason: The demonstrated decoding provides a basis for the proposed impact, while broader two-way restoration remains unachieved in the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Added roster-wide comparisons as labeled synthesis and preserved article-access and freshness limitations.
change_log.reason: The record needs to distinguish related innovations and communicate the evidence boundary without inventing dependencies or later results.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish the field's latest status or whether later studies demonstrated additional two-way capabilities.
The magnitude and tractability of tissue response, power, neural-population access and chronic selective-stimulation constraints require additional evidence.
The study does not establish generalizability across participants, implant sites, electrode types or neurological conditions.
Long-term fatigue, device wear and the safety and utility of chronic neural sensory stimulation remain insufficiently evaluated in the supplied evidence.
Trial duration, cohort diversity, permitted assistance, functional success thresholds and acceptable maintenance burden remain to be operationally defined.
The functional information rate and selectivity needed to justify high bandwidth depend on the intended tasks and remain unspecified.
The publisher PDF was inaccessible in the supplied research; the record relies on the article text described in the validated review.
